messages.subject: Error in proj[1, 2] : subscript out of bounds
messages.subject_clean: Error in proj[1, 2] : subscript out of bounds
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I started working with CTMM a few weeks ago, and after a few days and stumbling around got it to work successfully. Using data I uploaded to movebank, I fly through the code without erros.

I am now returning to old code to rerun it and produce figures, but when I go to run my old code

PM20tel<-as.telemetry(PM20, timeformat="",timezone="UTC",projection=NULL,timeout=Inf,na.rm="row",
                      mark.rm=FALSE,drop=TRUE)

I get this error

"Error in proj[1, 2] : subscript out of bounds"

Google tells me that this means I am trying to access an array out of its boundary, but none of the fixes I have found seem to be appropriate for the dataset,

Any advice or help anyone can give would be hugely appreciated,

Cheers

Josh

messages.subject: ocurrence() error
messages.body_plain:
Dear all

I am trying to use the function occurrence(). However, I obtain an error that I am not able to understand: "Error in if (CTMM$error) { : argument is of length zero"

I suspected that this means that one of my individuals has not enough positions. However, when I run akde() function I have not similar problems.

I attach my script just in case could be useful

Thanks in advances!

Eneko

df<-as.data.frame(MYDATA)

#1
TL<-as.telemetry(df, timesformat="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", timezone = "UTC")

#2
TL <- lapply(TL,
             function(x) x[round(seq(1,
                                     nrow(x),
                                     length.out = 100),
                                 0),])

#3
GUESS <- lapply(TL,
                function(x) ctmm.guess(x,
                                       interactive=FALSE))

#4
FITS <- lapply(1:length(TL),
               function(i) ctmm.fit(TL[[i]],
                                    GUESS[[i]])
)

#5
names(FITS) <- names(TL)

#6
UDS <- akde(TL,
            FITS,
            weights = TRUE)

#7
BB<-occurrence(TL,FITS)

messages.subject: How to find variogram asymptote from model results
messages.subject_clean: How to find variogram asymptote from model results
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am using animal telemetry data to create 'hypervolume' objects (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/hypervolume/index.html). The hypervolume method uses a kernel density approach and so assumes independent observations. My goal is to use the ctmm package to determine the number of days at which the variogram asymptotes, and then filter the data based on that number of days in order to have independent observations. My question is, how do I recover this value from the model fit results?

My first thought was to use tau_p, but this does not seem right, based on the vignette (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ctmm/vignettes/variogram.html). In the Variograms section, it is stated that Cilla asymptotes at 20 days. Then, just a few lines later, in the "Variogram Fitting the Hard Way" section, the value used for tau_p is 6 days. I also see that in the section "Maximum likelihood", the OUF anisotropic model has tau_p of around 6 days. Finally, the value of tau seems to change dramatically depending on the model. For example, OU anisotropic has tau_p of 14 days. So, perhaps I need to recover the asymptote based on the model as well as the model parameters?

For my data, ctmm.select() finds that OUF anisotropic is the best fit, and has a tau_p of 3.5 hours (see code and results below). Should I thin my dataset to one observation every 3.5 hours, in order to achieve independent observations, or should I use a different number?

Thanks so much for the help!

Here is the code and some results:

animal <- as.telemetry(mydf)
#mydf is for one animal (white stork) for one breeding season (Apr to Aug).
#I filtered the dataset to only those observations that ACC indicates foraging activity.

nrow(animal) #2707
vg.animal <- variogram(animal)
GUESS <- variogram.fit(vg.animal, interactive= FALSE)

FIT <- ctmm.select(animal,
                           CTMM = GUESS,
                           method = "pHREML",
                           control=list(method="pNewton"))

plot(vg.animal, CTMM=FIT,family="serif", fraction = 0.005)

plot(vg.animal, CTMM=FIT,family="serif", fraction = 1)

summary(FIT)

$name
[1] "OUF anisotropic"

$DOF
     mean      area     speed
 305.9462  499.4797 1766.9179

$CI
                                low         ML       high
area (square kilometers)  74.218845  81.183273  88.455549
τ[position] (hours)        3.208536   3.570317   3.972890
τ[velocity] (minutes)      5.875644   6.321963   6.802185
speed (kilometers/day)   112.648703 115.337956 118.026350

messages.subject: Re: ocurrence() error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Eneko,

If you can message/email me a minimal working example (data and script) to reproduce the issue, then I can take a look at it. occurrence() should be slower than akde().

In current versions of the package (on GitHub) cor.min maintains the specified fraction of velocity correlation over the gap, meaning that within the gap the motion is relatively ballistic and gaps are no longer filled in when they are so wide that there is little knowledge of where the individual is going within.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: How to find variogram asymptote from model results
messages.subject_clean: How to find variogram asymptote from model results
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ben,

I haven't tested the code in forever, because we've yet to publish it, but there are some capabilities in the package to make 3D AKDEs by fitting a vertical movement model and feeding that into akde(). I haven't even gotten around to supplying plotting methods, though.

tau_p = 6 days does not mean that the variogram asymptotes at 6 days. This is an exponential decay timescale, and so for instance you get 95% decay at 3*tau_p.

The OU tau_p is very different for the buffalo because that model is very misspecified in that case. Visually, you can see that the OU variogram does not match as well as the OUF.

Thinning to 3.5 hours would decay autocorrelation to exp(-1)=37%. Thinning to 3*3.5 hours = 10.5 hours will decay autocorrelation to exp(-3)=5%.

Best,
Chris

messages.body_plain:
Hi Martin,

I added this feature to the master branch on GitHub, which you can install via devtools::install_github("ctmm-initiative/ctmm").
I also coded around an R bug in the data.frame column names.

But to get from a telemetry object to a data.frame you do not need to convert it to a SpatialPointsDataFrame, because the telemetry object is already based on the data.frame object.

Best,
Chris

messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

I want to calculate the overlap between two individuals c and d:

      GUESSc <- ctmm.guess(c,interactive=FALSE)
      FITSVFc <- ctmm.fit(c,GUESSc)

      b <- overlap(list(c,d),list(FITSVFc, FITSVFd))

but I get the error: Error in overlap(list(c, d), list(FITSVFc, FITSVFd)) : Inconsistent projections.

which is strange because both telemetry objects come from move objects with the same projection: proj = CRS("+proj=longlat + ellps=WGS84")

Thanks in advance,
Danai

messages.subject: Re: Error: Inconsistent projections
messages.body_plain:
Hi Danai,

ctmm analyses have to be performed in a projected coordinate system to get area in square meters and speed in meters per second. When you imported those move objects into ctmm, there should have been a warning that the data had to be projected. If you imported them separately, they would have gotten different automated projections. You can import them together or give them the same projection afterwards, such as

projection(c) <- median(list(c,d))
projection(d) <- median(list(c,d))

Best,
Chris
